narrative.overview:
The category standard, played straight at a high craft level. One person, often in bed in dim morning light, opens the app, sees the month and today's reading at a glance, taps one coral button to record the day, and reads the chart without hunting for controls. Everything in the working app serves that: soft white cards on a warm off-white ground, one coral accent, a neutral sans with tabular figures, and generous touch targets.

The interface stays quiet so the observations can speak. Colour in the interface means exactly one thing (coral: act here, you are here, this is selected); every other colour inside the working screens belongs to the recorded data and the chart. Depth is a single soft ambient lift under white cards and a deeper float under sheets. The one translucent material is the phone tab bar, frosted with a solid fallback.

Two decorative places, both requested by the user, frame that quiet core and carry no meaning. The **header bloom** is a flat pale blush band with a five-petal flower mark and, on wide screens, a thin botanical sprig. The **Home meadow** is the first screen for everyone: a field of hand-drawn gerberas on three sage hills under a blush sky, with the page's content set out below as white garden signs. It is both the public welcome page before sign-in and the signed-in Home. Nothing in either place is clinical, dark or technical, and neither carries medical or contraceptive styling.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white ground, white cards, one ambient shadow.
One coral accent, used for the primary action, selection, focus, today and the active tab; on Home only for Sign in.
Inter, self-hosted, tabular figures for every number that is compared; Rubik only for Home headlines and the welcome brand.
44px minimum controls, 52px action rows, 50px primary buttons on the phone dock, 52px Sign in pill.
Flowers are scenery in two fixed places; observation colours are data, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Coral is the only interface accent. It marks what to press, what is selected, where focus is, and where you are. On Home it appears only as the Sign in pill, focus rings and the hover underline of the Create account link; the demo calendar's selected day is Meadow Ink, not coral.

rules.name: The Scenery Rule
rules.body: Bloom and meadow colours are decoration only and never encode an observation, a state or a navigation target. Flowers are allowed in exactly two places: the header bloom and the Home meadow.

rules.name: The Bloom Stays Home Rule
rules.body: `--bloom-*` colours appear only in the app header, the phone map title row and the welcome brand mark; `test/css-tokens.test.js` enforces it.

rules.name: The Meadow Stays on Home Rule
The Data Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Observation colours appear only where they encode a recorded observation or a chart tool's mark. Never use them for navigation, emphasis, illustration or brand.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: A colour the chart draws lives in `tokens.css` first and is mirrored in `chart-palette.js`; change both or neither.

rules.name: The Token Source Rule
rules.body: Every hex colour lives in `styles/tokens.css`; other stylesheets reference tokens (tested).

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader compares across rows or days (temperature, date numerals, times) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The rem Rule
rules.body: Text sizes are in rem so they follow the reader's text setting; container-query clamps are allowed only inside fixed-size cells, and the Home hero headline's clamp keeps rem bounds.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Rubik belongs to Home headlines and the welcome brand only; every working screen, control and number stays in Inter.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: A card has one shadow and keeps it on hover; hover shows as a soft border or a sunken fill, never as a card jumping up. Coming-soon signs carry no shadow at all.

rules.name: The Single Glass Rule
rules.body: The phone tab bar is the only translucent surface: 78% white, `saturate(1.6) blur(20px)`, solid white without `backdrop-filter` support or under `prefers-reduced-transparency`. Project tests forbid gradients and glass everywhere else except the time-picker drum's fade. The header band, sky and hills are flat colour.

dos: **Do** use coral (#c84a32) for exactly one primary action per view, the selected day, focus, today and the active tab, and on Home only for Sign in.
**Do** keep observation colours bound to recorded data and chart tools; add a new chart colour to `tokens.css` and `chart-palette.js` together.
**Do** put content on white 22px cards with the one Card shadow on the warm ground.
**Do** keep every colour value in `styles/tokens.css` and reference it by token.
**Do** keep bloom colours in the header, the phone map title row and the welcome brand, and meadow colours on Home.
**Do** keep controls at least 44px tall and set text in rem.
**Do** use tabular figures for temperatures, dates and times.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-contrast: more` and `prefers-reduced-transparency`, each with a real fallback; decorative motion must end on its own.
**Do** change appearance by toggling CSS classes; never write inline styles from JS.
**Do** check every change at about 320px, 390px and desktop width.
donts: **Don't** bring back the notebook look: cream paper, pastel or peach button fills, hairline-boxed day cells.
**Don't** use observation colours for decoration, navigation, brand or emphasis.
**Don't** let a bloom or meadow colour, or a flower, encode an observation, a state or a fertility meaning.
**Don't** draw flowers anywhere except the header bloom and the Home meadow.
**Don't** add gradients or glass anywhere except the time-picker drum fade and the phone tab bar.
**Don't** lift cards on hover or stack a second shadow inside a card.
**Don't** use Rubik outside Home headlines and the welcome brand.
**Don't** add medical or contraceptive styling, fertility verdict colours, hearts, or gamification.
**Don't** add uppercase eyebrow or kicker labels above titles; a state goes on the sign as a corner tag.
**Don't** make the interface dark, clinical or technical.
